newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt criticises Turkish buffer zone plans.
newsitem.headline: Egypt criticises Turkish buffer zone plans.

text.p: Egypt on Friday criticised Turkish plans to create a security buffer zone in Kurdish northern Iraq, saying all states should respect Iraqi sovereignty and hinting the U.N. Security Council should act to stop Turkey.
"We hope this is not true because encroaching on Iraqi territory in this way sets serious precedents," Foreign Minister Amr Moussa told reporters on his return from a trip abroad.

"Iraqi territorial integrity must be respected by all states including Turkey. If the U.N. Security Council takes a stand on Iraqi movements inside Iraqi territory, it should all the more take a stand on any other movements," he added.
"Northern Iraq should not be a free-for-all for any powers because that would invalidate the concept of Iraqi territorial integrity and sovereignty," he said.
Turkey is planning to create a security zone up to 10 km (six miles) deep in north Iraq and Washington said on Wednesday it would not object if Ankara went ahead with the scheme.
Moussa also welcomed the cancellation of a conference of Islamists which was to have taken place in London on Sunday.
Egypt has been campaigning against the conference, which it describes as a meeting of terrorists. The organisers said they could not afford the extra security costs.
"That's for the best, both for them and for us," Moussa said of the cancellation.
